note: Attacker controls the first 6 bytes of input, parsed as three int16 values for angle, x_center, y_center.

code: Pix* pix = pixReadMem(reinterpret_cast<const unsigned char*>(data), size);
note: Remaining bytes are passed as a BMP image buffer to pixReadMem, which dispatches to pixReadMemBmp.
Allocates cmapBuf with size = cmapEntries * 4 bytes, where cmapEntries is derived from the BMP header offset field.
Creates a PIXCMAP with nalloc = 1 << L_MIN(d, 8) and allocates an internal array of that many RGBA_QUAD entries.
Frees the internal array that pixcmapCreate allocated, leaving cmap->array as a dangling pointer.
Replaces cmap->array with cmapBuf, but cmap->nalloc is NOT updated; it still holds 1 << L_MIN(d, 8) while cmapBuf may have a different number of entries.
Sets cmap->n to the number of colormap entries read from the BMP, which can be larger than cmap->nalloc.
Assigns the colormap (with stale nalloc and mismatched array size) to the pix.

code: pixd = pixVShear(NULL, pixs, xcen, angle / 2., incolor);
note: First shear operation creates a new pix via pixCreateTemplate, which copies the colormap via pixCopyColormap -> pixcmapCopy.

code: cmapd->array = (void *)LEPT_CALLOC(1, nbytes); memcpy(cmapd->array, cmaps->array, cmaps->n * sizeof(RGBA_QUAD));
note: Allocates nbytes = cmaps->nalloc * sizeof(RGBA_QUAD) but memcpy reads cmaps->n entries. If cmaps->n > cmaps->nalloc, memcpy reads past the allocated cmapBuf boundary, causing heap-use-after-free READ.

The source cmaps->array points to cmapBuf which was allocated for cmapEntries entries, but cmaps->n may be larger than cmapEntries (capped at 256), and cmaps->nalloc is stale. When cmapEntries < cmaps->n, the memcpy reads freed/heap memory beyond the allocation.
